title: Verification receipt
description: What a domain's verification adapter returns. A receipt is evidence about the artifact THAT EXISTS NOW — hence artifact_sha256, which the exit gate re-checks against the live file. Staleness is the central attack on any verification pipeline: a passing run from a previous edit trivially launders a later broken artifact.

target_sha256.description: Must equal the frozen target hash.

artifact_sha256.description: The artifact's content hash AT VERIFICATION TIME. Re-hash the live artifact at the exit gate; if it differs, this receipt is stale and the artifact is unverified regardless of what the log says.

tier.description: Which adapter tier produced this. Must be a tier the pack declared, and must be the tier the work item froze.

produced_at.description: ISO-8601. Must be after the artifact's last modification.

refute_attempt.description: How the refute-attempt gate was discharged. Required — a result that survives only one favorable run does not earn a receipt.

discharged_by.description: adversarial_tier: the backend itself cannot be talked into a false pass. perturbed_rerun: re-run under a deliberately harsher condition. skeptic_pass: a dedicated attempt to break the result.

perturbation.description: Required in spirit for perturbed_rerun: what was made harder — a different seed, a tightened tolerance, a held-out split, a perturbed model.

completeness.description: A receipt is complete only when every obligation has a verdict, the concluding step is covered, and nothing is open or rejected. Truncated backend output is flagged, not read optimistically.

suspiciously_incomplete.description: Set when the backend output looks truncated. A truncated pass is not high assurance.

environment.description: How reproducible this run was. A receipt from a fresh process on a fresh copy in a restricted environment is worth more than one from a warm, mutable workspace.

log_excerpt.description: Backend output. Diagnostic evidence, not a paraphrase of it.

payload_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of this packet with payload_sha256 removed: sorted keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes. Seals the packet and makes it addressable by later packets — an id alone is a mutable label.

max_status.description: The strongest status this receipt could ever support — the ceiling of the tier that produced it. Required, because without it the reducer cannot enforce a ceiling from the evidence and has to take the granted status on trust. A pack whose backend tops out below VERIFIED says so here, and the reducer refuses anything above it.
